newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao told to quit last Congress party post.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao told to quit last Congress party post.

text.p: Leaders of India's Congress party on Wednesday asked former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, charged in three corruption cases, to step down from his last post in the nation's oldest party.

Rao, who led Congress to its worst defeat in general elections earlier this year, resigned as party president in September after a court summoned him to testify in a criminal conspiracy case. He denied any wrongdoing.
He has refused to relinquish his post as head of the party's parliamentary bloc, called the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP), where he has retained considerable political clout.
Twenty-one members of the CPP's executive committee and three office bearers asked Rao to quit in the interests of strengthening the party.

"We the elected members of the executive committee of the Congress Parliamentary Party...feel the need of change in the leadership of the CPP and request the leader to step down," the committee's members said in a resolution.
Rao said he would consider the request.
"I will consider the letter," CPP member Praful Patel quoted Rao as saying.

The resolution marked a final assault on Rao to resign from the post as head of the group that has a total strength of 229 legislators, 140 of whom are from the 545-member lower house, or Lok Sabha. The rest are in the upper house.
The unprecedented request by the Congress leaders, who included some of Rao's closest loyalists, was widely expected to force the former prime minister to quit.
"Either way is possible. Anything is possible," Subbarami Reddy, a CPP executive member, told Reuters. Reddy was considered close to Rao, but joined others on Wednesday in asking the leader to quit.
Newspapers said a struggle was already under way to select a replacement for Rao, who reached the pinnacle of power in 1991 after former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated.
The move to oust Rao was widely believed to be supported by Sitaram Kesri, who succeeded Rao as party chief in September.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said CPP members gave a copy of their resolution to Kesri, who planned to invite its office-bearers to a meeting of the Congress Working Committee (CWC), a powerful decision-making body, later in the day.
The meeting at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) was scheduled to discuss the Indian economy, but the leaders were invited to discuss the leadership issue if it arose at the meeting, PTI said.

Rao has been charged in three separate corruption cases which carry maximum penalties of seven years in jail if he is convicted. He has denied any wrongdoing, but his critics say the cases have tarnished the party's image.

Despite the humiliating loss at the polls, Rao has remained head of the parliamentary delegation that offers make-or-break support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party coalition that won power in June.
The resolution praised "the valuable services rendered by the respected leader during his tenure which has enabled the country to overcome deep economic crisis".
But it said the party needed to be strengthened.
"In this context it has become absolutely necessary to establish credibility of the party in the eyes of the people as this has suffered much due to recent happenings," it said.
